questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To me, the fact that Singapore is a very multicultural state was a decisive reason for me to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Singapore is very informative and they have things under control

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They are very good at informing you where to go and where to seek help if needed. I was given very thorough explanations about everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different actually. You can apply for different type of rooms - with and without aircon - but you are not guaranteed to get what you wish for or anything at all. All though, all my friends were lucky to get a room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can apply for rooms both with and without meal plans. The ones without have common cooking facilities

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a very good way to safe money as it is much cheaper than what else is offered in Singapore. But, it is not very luxurious. I was a bit sceptical at first but ended up being very happy I chose to live like this. it also has many social advantages to live on campus, I would say.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There a re many steps to go through and you have to really want to go

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It is easy to get help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. But I think it really depends on what courses you are interested in. Some are much harder to get than others.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry. Even though it can seem like a lot it is easy to seek help and the process often seems more stressful than it actually is.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level at NUS is high. But a lot of course details are offered on their webpage about courses. This helped pick courses that matched my priorities

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Instead of having one final exam, there are several tests/assignments during the semester that together form your final grade. Also, in some classes they use bell-curve to grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Gender and Islam, Introduction to Sikhism, South Asia in Singapore and Lifestyle, Behaviour and Public Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: South Asia in Singapore really taught me a lot about Singapore society and Asia in general.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. I think they are good at informing you

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries is really expensive. Local food is cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports and other activities. I lived right next to swimming pools, tennis courts and sports halls

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tennis

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed visiting nearby countries

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There are many exchange students and people from all over the world so even though moving to Asia is a big change I didn't find it too difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and courses with group work (they typically describe so in the course details)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The school mentality. People spend a lot of time on school and at school.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you go on exchange solely to have fun and not to go to school I think Singapore might be a place to reconsider. It is a highly ranked school and many people care a lot about their studies. Especially if you live on campus as well, it is all very 'school-centered'.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It provides you with so many great opportunities to experience and learn about other cultures, even though you are not taking classes about this topic. You are living in a multi cultural hub.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met. I think, because you are so far away from home, you quickly bond with the other people from your home university. I made friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not knowing what expectations are set by the school to pass classes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
